methodology_note: Study units derived from Toronto Notes SOURCE STRUCTURE (toc_inventory.json / derived/scope_packets/ID.json), cross-verified against the canonical raw-OCR corpus (derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/) given this chapter's unusually heavy TOC-extraction corruption. Chapter ID has 75 source nodes, 0 unresolved_headings per the deterministic packet, but raw-OCR verification found six distinct structural defects, the most severe found in any completed chapter to date: (1) ID.S04's printed title 'Gastrointestinal Infections' is body-confirmed (pdf 731/ID13) to be a pure cross-reference-only entry (see Gastroenterology G13/G18/G19/G31, Pediatrics P44) with zero independent content; the genuine 'Bone and Joint Infections' section (Septic Arthritis, Diabetic Foot Infections, Osteomyelitis) that TOC extraction merged into the same node is represented separately (SU-ID-06 REFERENCE_ONLY; SU-ID-07 DIRECT). (2) ID.S07 ('Systemic Infections') is missing a genuine T-child, 'Cat Scratch Disease', confirmed via raw OCR at pdf 741-742/ID23-24 within the section's own declared range; its title was instead concatenated onto the unrelated node ID.S17 (SU-ID-16). (3) A substantial 'Syphilis' section (pdf 742-743/ID24-25) has NO toc_inventory.json node at all - a more severe gap than any prior chapter's Fibroids/Sickle-Cell precedent, since even a mislabeled node does not exist - represented as UNCATALOGUED:ID.SYPHILIS (SU-ID-17). (4) ID.S08 'Tuberculosis' is recorded with a 7-page range (pdf 743-749) that actually spans two chapter topics: TB itself occupies only pdf 743-744/ID25-26 (SU-ID-18), and the remaining pdf 745-749/ID27-31 is a substantial, genuine HIV/AIDS section (Epidemiology, Etiology, Modes of Transmission, Natural History, diagnostic approach, Antiretroviral Drugs) that has no node of its own at its true location. (5) The largest single defect in this chapter: nodes ID.S17 through ID.S23 (toc-recorded at pdf 764-778/ID46-60, HIGH-confidence TOC_OCR titles) are a two-column TOC merge spanning nearly a third of the chapter's page range. Their titles concatenate genuine HIV disease-topic subheadings (HIV/Epidemiology/Modes of Transmission/Natural History, confirmed at pdf 745-749/ID27-31 -> SU-ID-19; Prevention of HIV Infection/Types of Testing/HIV Pre- and Post-Test Counselling, confirmed at pdf 749-750/ID31-32 -> SU-ID-20) with an unrelated antimicrobial-reference-appendix column (Antimicrobials/Antibiotics/Antifungals/Antiparasitics/Landmark Trials/References, confirmed at their toc-recorded pdf 764-778/ID46-60 -> SU-ID-32). Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever and West Nile Virus (part of ID.S18's title) were searched for as standalone body headings across the full chapter and not found; only table-row mentions exist within the Travel Medicine exposure table (SU-ID-29), so no separate RMSF/WNV unit is fabricated. The 'Syphilis' fragment of ID.S19's title is confirmed to be a recurring antibiotics-table column header, not a second real disease section (the genuine Syphilis content is the separate uncatalogued unit in finding 3). (6) ID.S09 ('FUNGALINFECTIONS'/'Skin and Subcutaneous Infections') and ID.S14 ('Ectoparasites'/'TravelMedicine') each follow the same pattern as finding (1): a cross-reference-only stub (Superficial Fungal Infections/Dermatophytes -> Dermatology; Ectoparasites/scabies/lice -> Dermatology D33) merged with a substantial real section (Subcutaneous Fungal Infections/Sporotrichosis; Travel Medicine), both confirmed at pdf 750/ID32 and pdf 759/ID41 respectively. Similarly, ID.S10's printed title 'Endemic Mycoses' (matching its own real content, Histoplasma/Blastomyces/Coccidioides at pdf 751/ID33) is merged with its merged_duplicate_headings entry 'Opportunistic Fungi' (PJP/Cryptococcus/Candida/Aspergillus, its actual T-children, at pdf 752-753/ID34-35) - both real, adjacent sections represented as two units (SU-ID-21, SU-ID-22) sharing one node, per the GY-Fibroids/H-Sickle-Cell dual-unit precedent. All six findings were resolved via the canonical clean-ocr corpus (derived/toronto-notes-2025/clean-ocr/, pdf pages 719-778), never via raw pdftotext of the source PDF directly (which was found to be substantially noisier/less reliable for this densely two-column-formatted chapter) and never via model memory. No heading was invented: the one genuinely uncatalogued topic (Syphilis) is marked with a synthetic UNCATALOGUED: id per the established project convention, and the RMSF/West Nile Virus title-fragments that could not be body-confirmed are documented as unresolved in review_items.json rather than represented as fabricated study units.

Per the rule against inventing headings, this well-evidenced but uncatalogued content is represented with a synthetic node id (UNCATALOGUED:ID.SYPHILIS), following the established convention used for chapter H's References bibliography (SU-H-51) and similar cases in chapters A/D/FM.
